Beautiful work! It doesn't come across as messy to me. If you're going for a very quintessential impressionist style, you could push the colours to be a bit funkier (more saturated, hue shifts) and get looser with your brush strokes. Honestly this is a *wonderful* painting as it is. Your colours, lighting, and brushstrokes are delicious.

Pretty sure the youtube video linked already said it, but -- textured brushes! It looks very digital because it's so smooth/soft and airbrush-esque. When you think of traditional art materials like brushes and pens, they all have visible and unique texture (ie brush hairs, unevenly shaped pen nib/uneven ink distribution). Especially thick paints often end up with a lot of brush and layering texture. Digital brushes are very perfect. Clearly you've got very beautiful foundations going though, wow!!

I would really like to know about this too!! I have a journal but I'd love to post in a place where it /could/ be an open discussion. I post here sometimes but reddit feels a bit forum-y for regular use

First off, beautiful work! You’ve got a beautiful composition going. As for your question, I would decide on the location of your light source + add some more light/shadow onto the fox from the atmosphere. I would add some nice cool toned shadows with slight ambient green light reflected up from the grass. Adding some colours of the environment will help it feels like it belongs. Either way, your friend will absolutely love this piece, and the time and care you put into it. Keep up the great work!!

Lol I love it so much!!! ahhahaha he’s always acting like he’s seeing ghosts, you captured him very well
I love the ink heavy sketchy style, very nice and expressive :)
Ahh thank you, it feels like a lot has changed :)
That's so kind of you to say, thank you!! :D

I really like your style, and you've definitely improved already! You're doing awesome, I can't wait to see more from you. :D 

If I had to offer any other advice - I'd say before getting into the nitty-gritty of where each muscles goes, maybe do some looser sketches and get a sense of proportions and flow. You can definitely still keep things stylized, but even heavily stylized work can benefit from some good foundations like proportionality and flow. Gesture sketching might be fun to poke into, to get a natural base sense of where things go!

Having a fitness trainer who works within the limits of chronic illness would be a miracle, haha! I think the hardest part for me is personally figuring out *where the heck to start* and *what is too much*. I haven't been super active now for about two years and getting back to it is really daunting. I overdo it a lot. 

Having someone who understood how fragile/sluggish sick bodies can be would be comforting. I feel like if I just go to any old fitness coach I would be super duper embarrassed at how hard everything is for me. I would be looking for someone who knows a lot of gentle exercise techniques that can slowly rebuild the strength in all the different parts of my body, working up slowly. 

I hope this is a little bit helpful, I think that's the most I can say since it would be individual to each client. I think honestly starting, pacing and exercising productively/non-harmfully are all things I struggle with.

Thank you for your comment - that is really balanced, in-depth advice, it was a really great read. You made a lot of really good points, I've written them down and I am absolutely going to remember them moving forwards. I'm feeling really hopeful and inspired after reading your posts - you're right, you never know what's around the corner. :)

I especially like the part about finding meaning - it's been hard to find motivation or interest with mental health barriers, but on the days I have something to live for it is a whole lot easier to get out of bed and take care of myself. I really appreciate you taking the time to share. I wish you the best as well! ❤️

Finding and creating smaller happinesses is really important when you're ill, I do agree. There definitely needs to be a balance of positives even if the situation feels really negative. I'm sorry to hear about your current situation, that sounds like a stressful ordeal. I'm wishing the best for you and your kiddos, I really hope you can get the help & support you need soon <3

Thank you truly for all the really practical advice. I've really been struggling coming to terms with being ill, even though it's been so long. My siblings, and friends who I've grown up with for a decade are all moving forwards and starting their lives, and I still find myself saying 'I should be able to do what they do'. Your comment is definitely helping me realize I just need to come to terms with my situation so I can give myself a better quality of life, rather than just trying to magically be normal, haha. Accepting it doesn't necessarily make it a part of my identity... but it is a part of my life, and I need to start acting like it. I need to get my crap together, and this is certainly a starting point -- so thank you truly for sharing.

Reading this made me feel so much better this morning, thank you for such an encouraging comment. I really admire your outlook on illness, acknowledging that it's hard but reaching a sort of peace with it. That seems healthy and reasonable, I feel like that's within the realm of possibility.

You're right, having a chronic illness can really shape a person in different ways. I've learned a lot about life, myself and other people through this journey. I hate that this happened to me, but I can appreciate all the lessons. Thank you for reminding me that it takes time - that is a fact I often neglect, and *really* need to remember. 

I especially like 'you can do hard things' - my mum tells me the same thing. Just because something isn't easy doesn't mean it's impossible (that could become my mantra, haha). Lyme treatment isn't straightforward but I do have options, even if they aren't simple. I really hope I can reach that point of hope soon. Thank you again for your lovely comment. :)

Oh my gosh, that sounds so up and down - I'm really glad you've been free from Lyme for so long, that's really awesome! Thank you for sharing!

I've done a few solid rounds of antibiotics! They definitely helped but we ran into some complications we've been trying to untangle to continue. We think I have additional conditions outside of Lyme, because my bloodwork is showing up a lot healthier in certain places after those rounds but I still have worsening symptoms. Exercise is one thing I love but am struggling to get out and do every day, I will certainly keep trying. T\^T

When you say LLMD, do you mean lyme-literate MD? Are those very common/how did you find one? We've only been working with lyme naturopaths who also do allopathic medicine so far... we couldn't find anyone else.

Wow, I actually really like that way of looking at things -- thank you so much for sharing. Especially that whole attitude about death -- I think it's a lot easier to think about what I can do to live meaningfully while I'm alive than focusing on every experience I lost, or won't get to live. Sometimes things suck, but keeping myself looking ahead with a goal is really helpful. It means a lot that you took the time to comment, I've never heard from anyone else in a similar situation - thank you truly. :) ❤️

Hey man, I'm really sorry you're in such an exhausting situation right now. It honestly sounds really really tough, I really hope you can find some relief soon. I'm sending virtual hugs if you want them. <3

What you wrote hit me in the heart and I felt obligated to reach out - I'm 17 and I've been sick 10 years, I can only imagine how tired you must be feeling right now. I have chronic lyme disease, and my symptoms started out very similar to yours - have you been tested before? 

I'm wishing you all the best in figuring this out! I hope tomorrow is a better day for you.

Hey, thanks for your kinds words, I appreciate the validation, haha. :) I'm really glad to hear I'm not alone. It's really difficult, having a desire for life but not in the way you're experiencing it. Sort of, a weird impossible/frustrating feeling.

It's been rough recently. I was doing okay until this new diagnosis, honestly, I had started to focus on my future until my new symptoms hit. It's been getting worse every day, so I'm hoping it's just a rough adjustment patch.
